links.outcome: Red flag recognition across four LLMs on neuropathic pain vignettes
links.effect: Significant between-model differences in safety outcomes including red flag recognition (p = 0.022); effect sizes small to moderate; diagnostic accuracy 92.5%-100% with no significant differences.
links.quote: In contrast, significant between-model differences emerged in clinical reasoning (p < 0.001), referral accuracy (p = 0.041), safety outcomes including red flag recognition (p = 0.022), readability (p < 0.001), and confidence scores (p < 0.001), with with effect sizes indicating small to moderate differences across domains.

links.outcome: Confidence calibration of LLM diagnostic responses
links.effect: All models underconfident in aggregate; overconfidence in incorrect responses in some models; confidence scores differed significantly between models (p < 0.001).
links.quote: At the aggregate level, all models demonstrated underconfidence; however, overconfidence in incorrect responses was observed in some models.

unlisted_practices: Multidimensional evaluation framework beyond diagnostic accuracy (reasoning, safety, referral, readability, calibration) before real-world use

screen.reason: The study evaluates the diagnostic performance, reasoning, and safety of several LLMs on standardized clinical vignettes for neuropathic pain without testing a specific organizational guardrail or deployment practice.
